title: Single-use local `min_approvers` in haute_toml adds no value
description: haute_toml() defines `min_approvers = 2` (line 221) only to interpolate it once as `min_approvers = {min_approvers}` in the f-string (line 243). The local is assigned once and read once; inlining the literal (`min_approvers = 2` directly in the template body) removes the indirection without changing output. Minor, but it is a one-use temporary that obscures rather than clarifies.
evidence: Line 221 `min_approvers = 2`; line 243 `min_approvers = {min_approvers}` inside the f-string — the only use.
behavior_preservation: Inlining the constant yields byte-identical TOML; test_team_defaults (asserts 'min_approvers = 2') and all TOML-parse tests still pass.
